metadata.title: Smoke in the Cabin (Placeholder)
metadata.description: PLACEHOLDER: A smoke indication scenario for flight training. This scenario is a structural scaffold only — no real procedures are encoded. It demonstrates the schema extension points for aircraft state, weather, failures, and ATC communication.
metadata.author: PiperScenarioLab (Placeholder)

pre_flight.name: Pre-Flight / Climb Phase
pre_flight.description: PLACEHOLDER: Aircraft is in climb phase. A smoke indication is reported from the cabin. This act would contain the initial assessment and response procedures in a real scenario.

cockpit.name: Cockpit
cockpit.description: PLACEHOLDER: Flight deck environment. In a real scenario, this would include ECAM displays, overhead panel state, and systems indications. The pilot must assess the smoke report and coordinate with cabin crew and ATC.

aviate.description: PLACEHOLDER: Maintain aircraft control. In a real scenario, this would involve fly the aircraft first — maintain attitude, airspeed, and altitude as appropriate to the situation.

navigate.description: PLACEHOLDER: Determine position and plan routing. In a real scenario, this would involve assessing nearest suitable airport, terrain, and weather considerations.

communicate.description: PLACEHOLDER: Communicate with ATC and cabin crew. In a real scenario, this would involve MAYDAY/PAN-PAN call, cabin crew coordination, and passenger PA as appropriate.

motives: Provide assistance to aircraft in distress
persona.speech_style: Standard ICAO phraseology. Clear, concise, no extraneous words. Prioritizes safety-critical information.
Direct and factual. Reports symptoms clearly. Uses standard crew communication protocol. Acknowledges commands promptly.
